title: The Swan, the Pike and the Crayfish
text:
Ivan Krylov opens this fable with a warning: when partners are not in agreement, things go badly for them, and nothing comes of their work but trouble.

One day a swan, a pike and a crayfish decided to pull a cart loaded with goods. They harnessed themselves to it, all three together, and set to work with great effort. They strained and pulled with all their might. The load was not especially heavy, and with three strong animals pulling, the job should have been easy.

But the cart did not move an inch. The swan pulled upward, toward the clouds. The pike pulled toward the water. The crayfish, as crayfish do, crawled backward. Each was working hard, and each was sure the others were to blame.

Who was right and who was wrong, Krylov remarks, is not for us to judge. All that is known is that the cart is still standing there to this day.
lesson: Effort is wasted when a team pulls in different directions. Before working harder, make sure everyone agrees where the cart is going.
people: A swan, a pike, a crayfish
source: Ivan Krylov, Fables (Basni), The Swan, the Pike and the Crayfish (Lebed, Shchuka i Rak), 1814
